newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to draw on coffee stocks for exports.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to draw on coffee stocks for exports.

text.p: Colombia, which is expected to experience an 11.7 percent drop in parchment coffee production this year, will draw on internal stocks to meet its export commitments abroad, Foreign Trade Minister Morris Harf said.
"We will meet the export target of 12 million (60 kilo) bags by drawing on the National Coffee Fund's inventories," Harf said.
He said this would help guarantee more than $2 billion in 1996 coffee export earnings despite the sharp in production, due at least in part to unusually heavy rains.

Harf spoke in an interview with Caracol radio station early Thursday, hours after the Finance Ministry and National Planning Department said parchment coffee production fell 5.9 percent during the first half of the year and was expected to drop another 5.8 percent by year's end.
The decline comes on top of a huge 33.8 percent drop in parchment coffee production during the second half of 1995.

It takes 1.3 lbs of parchment coffee to produce a single pound of excelso. Harf did not specify what amount of coffee would be drawn from the National Coffee Fund's stocks to meet the 12-million-bag export target.
